questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Niger?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Niger on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Niger article.

questions.proof: The longest border is with Nigeria to the south.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Niger about 1,267,000 square kilometres; Gabon about 267,667 square kilometres; Portugal about 92,225 square kilometres; Sierra Leone about 71,740 square kilometres.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Niger on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Niger on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Niger?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Niger article.

questions.proof: The capital is Niamey, and the official language is Hausa.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Niamey?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Niger is Niamey.
